subject: Procurement prep: security package (SOC 2, audit logs, demo tenant isolation) — Aurora Fintech

Subject: Procurement prep: security package (SOC 2, audit logs, demo tenant isolation)

Hi Hannah,

As part of our early procurement/security prep, can you share the following for Redwood Inference?

1) SOC 2 Type II report and/or a SOC 2 attestation letter (and bridge letter if applicable)
2) Audit log details: what events are captured, retention, and export options (SIEM)
3) A short description we can reuse internally describing how your sales demo tenant is isolated/sanitized (we want to confirm no other customer data is involved)

If you have a standard “security package” PDF we can start there.

Thanks,
Dana

Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement prep: security package (SOC 2, audit logs, demo tenant isolation) — Aurora Fintech

Audit logging details you can share externally (safe/accurate for Hosted + Dedicated; for Private we’ll align to their SIEM stack during implementation):

What we log (examples):
- Admin + user authentication events (login, SSO assertions when enabled)
- Access control changes (role assignment/removal)
- API key lifecycle events (create/revoke/rotate)
- Control plane/config changes (model pinning/version changes, route/routing policy updates, fallback policy changes, quota/rate-limit config)
- Usage events at the tenant level (request metadata + token counts; content logging is configurable)
- Operational events relevant to incident review (e.g., rate-limited requests, 5xx errors)

Retention:
- Default demo/hosted retention is 30 days in Console.
- Longer retention available for enterprise plans (and Private depends on customer storage/retention policy).

Export:
- Console supports audit log export via API.
- For enterprise, we support forwarding audit logs to customer systems (commonly Splunk/Datadog/Sumo) via supported integration patterns; exact mechanism depends on deployment mode.

Important nuance: we can run with “safe logging” where prompt/output payloads are not retained (or are redacted); audit logs still capture the action/metadata.

If you want, I can also provide a 1-paragraph “audit log FAQ” summary for their security team.

Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
Audit Logging & SIEM Integrations | Redwood Inference



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement prep: security package (SOC 2, audit logs, demo tenant isolation) — Aurora Fintech

Here’s demo tenant isolation/sanitization language (feel free to paste verbatim). This matches our internal demo tenant FAQ.

“Redwood’s standard sales demo runs in a dedicated internal ‘demo tenant’ that is logically isolated from all customer tenants. The demo tenant contains only Redwood-generated sample prompts and synthetic data (no customer content). Access is restricted to authorized Redwood employees via RBAC, and credentials are time-bound and rotated. Demo usage is monitored using the same observability controls as production tenants (latency, errors, throttles), and logging is configured for demo safety (no customer PII; prompt/output retention is controlled). The demo tenant is used solely for product demonstration; customer evaluations can be run in a separate trial tenant or in Dedicated/Private deployment modes depending on security requirements.”

If they ask about data residency: our standard demo tenant is hosted in US regions; we can talk through EU-only routing for production use cases separately.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference



From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement prep: security package (SOC 2, audit logs, demo tenant isolation)

Hi Dana (cc Ravi),

Thanks — sharing what we can right away and outlining the path for the SOC 2 report.

1) SOC 2 Type II
- We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under mutual NDA.
- If you can confirm whether an NDA is already in place between Aurora Fintech and Redwood, we’ll either (a) share via secure link immediately, or (b) send our standard NDA for signature first.

2) Audit logs (summary)
Redwood maintains audit logs for key security and administrative actions including:
- Authentication events (login/SSO when enabled)
- Role/access control changes
- API key create/revoke/rotate
- Tenant configuration changes (routing/fallback policy updates, model version pinning, quota/rate-limit changes)
- Tenant-level usage metadata (including token counts) and operational events (e.g., rate limits, 5xx)

Retention/Export:
- Default retention for hosted/demo environments is 30 days in Console.
- Export is available via API; enterprise options include forwarding to common SIEM destinations (implementation depends on deployment mode).
- Logging can be configured for “safe logging” so prompt/output payloads are not retained (audit logs still capture the action/metadata).

3) Demo tenant isolation/sanitization (paste-ready)
“Redwood’s standard sales demo runs in a dedicated internal ‘demo tenant’ that is logically isolated from all customer tenants. The demo tenant contains only Redwood-generated sample prompts and synthetic data (no customer content). Access is restricted to authorized Redwood employees via RBAC, and credentials are time-bound and rotated. Demo usage is monitored using the same observability controls as production tenants (latency, errors, throttles), and logging is configured for demo safety (no customer PII; prompt/output retention is controlled). The demo tenant is used solely for product demonstration; customer evaluations can be run in a separate trial tenant or in Dedicated/Private deployment modes depending on security requirements.”

Attached: our standard Security Overview PDF (good for early-stage review).

If helpful, we can also set up a 20–30 min security walkthrough with our security/compliance team to align on audit logs + retention expectations before the evaluation starts.

Best,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Inference_Security_Overview_v2025-01.pdf (PDF)
